name: rejects a rotation the claimed old identity did not sign
note: The rotation says it hands off from new@ to other@, but the certificate says old@ signed it. Anchor refuses to reinterpret that as old@'s own handoff — a rotation is a statement by the identity named in oldIdentity, and nobody can authorize a handoff on a third party's behalf. Dropping it also closes the graft: an attacker who could publish a rotation naming themselves as the successor of a publisher they do not control would otherwise be chained into that publisher's lineage.
